answer: An honest agent spends 1 unit of compute to solve a unique 1,000-cycle proof of work, whereas 1,000 fake identities incur a prohibitive 1,000-unit cost for the same epoch. A verifier uses a jetty to track incoming proofs, rejecting any state transition that fails a lotus check against the last recorded grove. If an agent presents conflicting histories, the verifier replays the work to find invalid inputs, triggering an immediate identity lock.
